summary: The University of Illinois reply to a UCLA request for information on network graphics. It describes graphics support for application groups, including imitating the CALCOMP plotter package, producing output for the Network Graphics Protocol, and grey-scale work on several devices. It is an informal status report.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC answers a request for information about network graphics. Illinois describes its output formats, grayscale projects, and plans for interactive graphics.

subtitle: Illinois reports on graphics work and plans in response to a network survey.

tldr.problem: A UCLA request asked network sites for information about their graphics capabilities.
tldr.mechanism: Illinois describes graphics support based on CALCOMP-style plotting with NGP output, grayscale work, and a planned interactive system.
tldr.outcome: The reply records current work and design questions; it does not define a graphics standard.

sections.title: Graphics Work at Illinois
sections.content:
Steve Bunch's reply describes graphics work at Illinois, responding to Craig Maxwell's request for graphics information. For beam-oriented graphics, Illinois aimed to emulate the CALCOMP plotter support package while producing NGP0 output.

The RFC says some peripherals required conversion to device-specific formats, while planned local systems were expected to handle those conversions.
sections.plainLanguage: Illinois adapted a familiar plotter package to produce Network Graphics Protocol output. Some devices still needed their own output conversion.

sections.title: Grayscale and Interactive Graphics
sections.content:
The report describes grayscale work on GOULD and IMLAC systems for satellite pictures, natural-resource maps, and holograms. It says no standardization plans had been made for grayscale work.

A small group was planning an interactive graphics system using multiple hosts. A prototype was used for simple meteorological data manipulations, including contouring and three-dimensional plotting.
sections.plainLanguage: Different groups were using grayscale graphics for pictures, maps, and holograms. The RFC says there was no standardization plan for this work.

sections.title: Planned Commands and Design Choices
sections.content:
The author hoped to finish an IMLAC program that could interact with a mouse and keyset. The planned outgoing commands were MOVE, DRAW, TEXT, and UNDO, with further commands possible as needed.

The RFC discusses whether nodes should share a command set or distinguish between displays and computers. Bunch favors the first approach for its generality, while noting the simpler approach may help less capable devices.
sections.plainLanguage: The planned interface would include commands to move, draw, add text, and undo. The author favors a general shared command set but notes that simpler displays may need less.
